title: Where RL Will Take Search — Maximilian-David Rumpf, SID.ai
talk_summary: SID.ai argues that agentic search is 100-1000x more expensive and slower than classical search, and that RL-trained specialized search sub-agents can recover quality while being ~20x faster and ~100x cheaper. The core mechanism is delegating search to a sub-agent so the main agent's context only sees good results, plus RL on a verifiable reward (did you find the correct document).

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of the main agent doing retrieval and iterating through bad results, a dedicated sub-agent does all searching/reading/iterating and returns only a ranked list of good results to the main agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the bad stuff that it finds is essentially polluting its own context window... the main agent only ever sees great results
takeaways.numbers: agents spend 30-50% of tokens on searching

takeaways.technique: Route retrieval to cheapest capable model
takeaways.what_they_do: Offload the token-heavy search phase to a specialized cheap model rather than the frontier main model, since search doesn't need most of the LLM's general capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those 30 to 50% tokens that were earlier used by the main agent to do searching can now be passed off to this just you know 100x cheaper search sub agent
takeaways.numbers: ~100x cheaper, ~20x faster (2 min -> 5 sec) vs frontier model

takeaways.what_they_do: Define a grindable reward: for a given question, did the agent find the correct document? This makes retrieval quality measurable and improvable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Verifiable here means for a given question, did you find the correct document?

takeaways.what_they_do: A single RL model decides on the fly how much to search/iterate, spending more compute only on hard questions rather than a fixed budget per query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use much more compute if a user asks a very difficult question

takeaways.technique: Sub-agent returns only vetted results to gatekeeper
takeaways.evidence_quote: the main agent sees more good stuff, which means it's more likely to be correct
